annotations.text:
Direction: lean into the terminal identity the app already has.

Everything here uses the existing tokens — brand green #22c55e, gray-950 ground, gray-900 cards, gray-800 borders, JetBrains Mono for labels and the wordmark, rounded-xl cards. The only new ingredient is atmosphere: the faint grid, the brand bloom, and the 0 0 36px rgba(34,197,94,.08) glow already used on the editor panel, borrowed for the hero and solved cards.

1 — Logged-out hero

Today a signed-out visitor lands on the bare "Exercises" heading plus a login nag box. This gives the app a face: one headline, one primary CTA, and a vignette that shows the actual product doing its actual thing (editor + passing tests).

The three "How it works" cards are facts about your build — Monaco, Pyodide in-browser, server-side hidden tests — not invented stats.

2 — Filter bar + richer cards

New: the filter row (difficulty chips, unsolved-only toggle, search) and the section headers, which now carry a count and a per-category progress bar.

Cards now read at a glance: solved gets a brand-tinted border and glow, attempted gets a thin best-score bar in its own difficulty colour, untouched stays quiet. All three states use data already in useProgressStore — no backend work.

3 — Loading, empty, post-submit

Skeleton cards replace the lone spinner. The empty state is dashed, not red, so it doesn't read as the error card.

The post-submit panel is the one place worth adding data: User.total_score and User.streak come back from your API and are currently displayed nowhere in the app.
Hero at 390px. Headline drops 68px → 38px, CTAs go full-width, the vignette loses the line numbers and the overlapping score chip (it would clip). No fake status bar — the real one paints over this.

One thing to fix either way: index.html only loads JetBrains Mono at 400;500, but the wordmark and section heads ask for 600/700 — the browser is faking bold on them right now. Add 600;700 to the font URL.
